validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed by three independent sources. (1) WBI Energy, Inc./Marketwired press release (Sept 7 2016, via Yahoo Finance mirror) announcing the project moving to construction; (2) Natural Gas Intel trade-press article (Feb 15 2018, read via Wayback since the live URL now 404s) reporting the FERC order in Docket No. CP17-257 authorizing WBI to construct and operate the project; (3) EIA's federal 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' historical workbook, which carries a row for 'Valley Expansion Project' / operator 'WBI Energy Transmission', Project Type 'Expansion', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2018-10-31, Year In Service 2018, States MN/ND -- an independent government data source, not GEM-derived. All three name the pipeline explicitly and agree on route (Mapleton, ND to a Viking Gas Transmission interconnection near Felton, Clay County, MN), operator family (WBI Energy / MDU Resources), and 2018 completion. Not a phantom/GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly an interstate FERC-jurisdictional natural-gas transmission expansion (bi-directional firm transportation service between the Viking interconnection and the new Mapleton Compressor Station) -- not a gathering/distribution line. Operating status is directly confirmed (EIA 'Completed'), not merely inferred. DUPLICATE: checked against the roster's Williston/Bakken transmission cluster (P0158 Bison, P0281 Williston Basin, P2099 Northern Border, P3158 Traill County, P0306 Doosan Bobcat, P0316 South Saskatchewan Access) -- Valley Expansion's Mapleton-to-Felton/Viking-interconnection route and its own FERC docket (CP17-257) are distinct from all of those; no duplicate/relabel found. Of the row's 4 harvested wiki citations, opened and read 3 (PGJ Planned-Projects PDF, Yahoo Finance/Marketwired release, EIA data.php landing page + the actual EIA workbook it points to); could not open the 4th (Natural Gas Intel) at its live URL (404) and used its Wayback capture instead. The PGJ 'Planned Projects' PDF (Oct 2018 issue) does NOT mention this pipeline, WBI, or Mapleton anywhere in its text -- it is not usable as a ref (fails the name-must-appear rule) even though it was accessible.

validity.recommendation: verify and likely correct Capacity from 33 MMcf/d to ~40 MMcf/d (design/certificated capacity)
validity.researcher_notes: Both independent sources that state a capacity figure disagree with the sheet's 33.00 MMcf/d, and agree with each other: the Sept 2016 WBI/Marketwired press release states the pipeline 'is designed to transport 40 million cubic feet of natural gas per day,' and the Feb 2018 Natural Gas Intel article on the FERC order (Docket CP17-257) independently states 'the project is designed to provide about 40,000 Dth/d of firm natural gas transportation service' (40,000 Dth/d is essentially equivalent to ~40 MMcf/d). Both figures were stated at different times (project announcement vs. FERC authorization) by different publishers, so this is genuine 2-source corroboration on ~40, not one repeated wire story. I could not find any source stating 33 MMcf/d for this project, and could not determine whether 33 might reflect a different metric (e.g. actual subscribed firm capacity vs. nameplate/design capacity, or a later de-rating) -- I did not find a source for that alternative explanation either. Given the material size of the gap (33 vs ~40, about 21%) this is flagged as a spec concern rather than silently filled; the sheet's Capacity cell should be reviewed against the FERC order itself (Docket CP17-257, order ~162 FERC P 61,096, Feb 15 2018) before changing it, since I was not able to retrieve the order text directly (elibrary.ferc.gov's search interface is JS-driven and did not return results to a scripted fetch, and this session's web-search budget was exhausted before I could locate a mirrored copy).

validity.recommendation: Length (37.30 mi) and SegmentCost ($57M) are plausible and within the range independent sources give, but neither is confirmed to the exact digit -- treat both as REFS_ADDED at medium/high rather than exactly nailed down
validity.researcher_notes: Length: the 2016 WBI release states the pipeline is '38-mile' (a rounded pre-filing estimate); the 2018 Natural Gas Intel/FERC article separately states FERC required WBI to adopt the 'I-29 variation' of the route, 'even though the length of its proposed pipeline would increase by 0.2 miles.' Neither source gives 37.30 exactly, but the two together bracket a plausible final mileage in the high-37/38 range depending on what the pre-variation filed length was (I could not retrieve the FERC order text itself to get the precise figure -- see the Capacity note on why). 37.30 is consistent with, not contradicted by, these sources, so I am not filing this as a spec concern, but I'm also not claiming exact confirmation. Cost: both sources state the project cost was estimated at '$55 million to $60 million,' and the sheet's SegmentCost of $57,000,000 sits squarely inside that range -- treated as REFS_ADDED (fills below) rather than a concern.
